reviewed_behavior: The change is confined to GitHub.logs and requires a positive integer selected job. One authenticated API Request continues to address that same job throughout the call.
Every new signed attempt obtains a fresh redirect. The unchanged NoRedirect/API helper handles API responses separately; an API HTTP503 never enters the signed-download retry handler.

The signed request remains urllib.request.urlopen(target_string, timeout=120). API headers and credentials are not forwarded to that target. Existing HTTPS/hostname/no-userinfo redirect checks remain mandatory.

Only HTTP503 from the signed GET/read receives the new bounded policy. Other HTTP codes, timeout and transport failures continue to propagate. Complete bytes are returned only after a successful response.read(); no partial result is concatenated or promoted.

At most four signed requests are attempted, with 30/60/120-second minimum waits. The reviewed unchanged pure service-delay parser respects explicit Retry-After and existing millisecond headers; invalid or over-window waits stop.

The monotonic 600-second window is checked before a renewed redirect lookup, after redirect resolution, before waiting and after waiting. Existing API rate-limit waits do not reset this window; no subsequent signed GET starts after a long API wait exhausts it. The existing inline API200 return and in-flight timeout behavior are retained.
The new structured log rows bind the selected job ID and expose only fixed decisions/numeric waits/header-presence booleans, without URL, token, response body or raw header values.
The unchanged artifact helper is imported only for its pure wait parser. Its ZIP retry/restore behavior and the reviewed API 403/429/502 helper are not modified.

All selection, identity, origin, source, closure, output, axiom, receipt, restore and milestone code lies outside the changed method and is byte identical. Workflow steps/resources remain byte identical; only the collector push filter is added.

focused_mock_review.assessment: The mocks cover same-job fresh redirects, token confinement, attempt and wait bounds, service waits, long API rate waits, inline API200, unchanged redirect/status/transport handling and existing API helper integration. No additional runtime execution was needed.

actual_failure_basis.surface: signed job log GET after GitHub API302

conclusion: No concrete blocker remains in the exact two-file runtime delta. This review does not claim an actual retry outcome, complete collection, restored objects, kernel exports or family completion; the next publication and native run remain root-owned.
